accepted_scope: An exit is emitted only for a readable present current session entry with accepted audit backing, including supported legacy dangerous backing. Implicit/absent/corrupt fallback arbiter and unbacked raw markers create no synthetic prior operator event. A later departure from explicitly entered arbiter does get an exit. Same mode no-op remains no-op unless matching debt must settle.
strategy: Fresh transition exit+enter share an opaque 128-bit random NOTE identity and are staged together through existing max8 write-ahead queue. Exact saved bytes are replay identity, so historical same-second rows cannot satisfy a fresh failed transition. Existing legacy single-new-line callers/format remain supported. Entropy is an event identity, not a credential/authorization grant.
failure_truth: Marker write must verify before audit. Partial append retains remaining pair debt and same token retries it even with older requested-mode backing. Failed queue persistence plus failed audit can leave no durable debt; outcome stays failed/owed with owed_rows0 and explicit inspect/repair guidance instead of promising replay.
limits: The existing marker-before-audit interval is not an atomic multi-file transaction; a process crash before queue persistence can lose prior exit identity.

If both journal persistence and trail append are denied, future processes cannot reconstruct lost old-mode exit solely from the new marker. The explicit new control records this limit; no unconditional durable guarantee.
Existing bounded queue can discard oldest rows with its aggregate drop note. Cap remains8. Existing tail replay bound remains64KiB.

Existing shared pending-queue read/modify/write is not globally serialized across arbitrary concurrent sessions. This repair adds no universal queue-concurrency or hostile same-user filesystem guarantee.
Existing legacy backing acceptance is retained, not broadened or independently authenticated by this repair.
